summary: Intro call to understand Lacuna Health's latency and throughput targets for an LLM-powered triage assistant. Main blockers: p95 latency requirement for streaming responses, expected concurrency and peak tokens/sec, security/SOC2/KMS concerns. AE/SE to run initial benchmarks with customer's prompt set and share pricing + security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Collins (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie with Redwood - joining me from the engineering side is Sofia and Omar. Quick intro from you all?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Narang (CTO): Hi, Priya here, CTO at Lacuna Health. We run a clinical triage assistant we're trying to move from a prototype to production, need to understand latency and throughput tradeoffs.
[00:16] Evan Brooks (AI Eng): Evan, I own model infra. We currently run inference on SageMaker for a couple of models and also evaluate hosted APIs.
[00:22] Maya Chen (Platform): Hi, Maya, platform lead. Interested in deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:27] Jamie Collins: Great. Today's goal is to understand p95 targets, concurrency, streaming needs and whether Redwood hosted or Dedicated/Private makes sense. Sofia, do you want to kick off?
[00:34] Sofia Martinez (SE): Yeah thanks. Quick note — apologies if audio is fuzzy. Can you give us current numbers: p95 latency goal, typical tokens-per-request, and concurrency at peak?
[00:45] Evan Brooks: Sure. Our ideal p95 for user visible streaming responses is <300ms for system messages, but for full response maybe up to 800ms is acceptable. Typical prompts are 60-120 tokens, but we also have some longer context windows up to 2k tokens. Peak concurrency estimate is 50 concurrent users during clinic hours, but bursts to 120 for certain flows.
[01:05] Omar Aziz (SE): Got it — so streaming matters. When you say streaming, do you mean token-by-token streaming to the UI?
[01:12] Evan Brooks: Yes, exactly — incremental tokens as they're generated. We care about first-token latency (time to first token) and also p95 tail for continued streaming.
[01:20] Maya Chen: Also worth noting we need audit logs and KMS integration; data is PHI so we may need Private or VPC in future.
[01:28] Jamie Collins: Makes sense. Two routes typically: Redwood Hosted for fastest time to value and predictable per-token pricing, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools and stricter isolation, and Redwood Private for on-prem/VPC. For PHI with strict control you may be leaning Dedicated or Private.
[01:43] Dr. Priya Narang: Right. Can you clarify the p95 numbers you can hit on Dedicated versus Hosted?
[01:49] Sofia Martinez: Short answer: it depends on model size, quantization, and batching policy. For example, with a 7B quantized model on a Dedicated instance we commonly see first-token latencies in the 60-120ms range and sustained token generation at 250-700 tokens/sec depending on GPU. For p95 overall response latency for 60-120 token replies that often maps to sub-500ms p95 on Dedicated when streaming is enabled and batching is small. Hosted has similar profiles for bursty low-latency requests but can be subject to multi-tenant bursts unless you buy Dedicated.
[02:20] Evan Brooks: Curious about tokens/sec benchmarking — do you bench tokens/sec per GPU or per route? Our workload is mixed: lots of short requests and occasional long-generation sessions.
[02:29] Omar Aziz: We usually provide tokens/sec both per-GPU and an end-to-end tokens/sec for your route including network/serialization overhead. For short prompts our continuous batching engine tries to keep latency SLOs by limiting batching window — so tokens/sec gains are lower but latency is better. For long-running generations you get much higher tokens/sec.
[02:46] Maya Chen: What about concurrency? If we have 120 concurrent streaming sessions, do you create separate kernels or multiplex on GPUs?
[02:53] Sofia Martinez: We multiplex. The runtime uses token-slicing and KV cache multiplexing — each active session holds a KV state but can share compute when generating tokens. The key for p95 is controlling batching windows and dedicated capacity. For 120 concurrent short sessions aiming for p95 <800ms you likely need either Dedicated with autoscaled GPU pool or Hosted with a higher commitment. We'll model this after your prompt distribution.
[03:18] Dr. Priya Narang: Are there examples of customers in healthcare using Private deployment for PHI?
[03:24] Jamie Collins: Yes, we've done Private deployments with KMS integrations and SOC2 controls for a handful of regulated customers. We'll share case references and the security whitepaper.
[03:30] Leo Park (Security): We need clarity on audit logs retention, KMS key management, and whether Redwood touches plaintext. Also SAML SSO and RBAC.
[03:38] Jamie Collins: Under Dedicated/Private we can support customer-managed KMS and we provide immutable audit logs with configurable retention. For Hosted we offer SOC2 and AES-256 at rest, but KMS control is limited compared to Dedicated/Private. We'll attach the SOC2 summary.
[03:52] Evan Brooks: Back to benchmarking — can you run a p95 token latency test with our prompt set? We have a mix of 32-token questions and longer 512-1500 token contexts.
[04:01] Sofia Martinez: Yes. If you can share prompts we'll run three scenarios: 32-token short replies (low-latency), 128-token canonical replies (mixed), and long-context 1k+ generations. We'll report first-token latency, p95 total response latency, and tokens/sec under different concurrency levels (10, 50, 120).
[04:20] Evan Brooks: For concurrency modeling, we also want cost estimates — tokens/sec per dollar roughly.
[04:25] Jamie Collins: We'll produce a small TCO workbook comparing Hosted vs Dedicated (reserved) vs Private (license + infra), showing per-token cost with batching assumptions.
[04:33] Maya Chen: Any gotchas around streaming + function calling? We plan to use tool calls to internal APIs and then stream final answers.
[04:41] Omar Aziz: Function/tool calling is supported and can be combined with streaming — but tool calls introduce additional round trips. Typically we model them as additional synchronous steps; if you need sub-300ms p95 through entire tool call flow you'll likely want co-located endpoints and minimal network hops.
[04:58] Evan Brooks: How about fallbacks — if Dedicated is saturated do you fallback to smaller models hosted?
[05:04] Sofia Martinez: Yes, smart routing supports fallback policies — route to cheaper/compatible model variants or to Hosted when Dedicated is full. We also support per-route SLOs and automatic degrade to shorter context or lower-quality model.
[05:16] Dr. Priya Narang: For HIPAA compliance, data residency matters — do you support region pinning?
[05:21] Jamie Collins: We do region pinning for Hosted in supported regions, and Dedicated/Private gives you full control over region and VPC. We'll include the regions list in the follow-up.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Any initial sizing guidance? For 120 peak concurrent sessions with average 100 tokens per response and p95 target 800ms, ballpark how many GPUs?
[05:38] Sofia Martinez: Ballpark: depends on the model. For a 13B quantized optimized model you might need 4-6 A10/A100-class GPUs with autoscale headroom for peaks, but for a 7B optimized quantized model you could hit that with 2-3 GPUs. We'll run a simulation with your prompt distribution to better estimate.
[05:55] Evan Brooks: We'll provide the prompt set — should we anonymize PHI?
[05:58] Leo Park: Yes, send anonymized samples. We'll prepare a sanitized prompt dump.
[06:02] Jamie Collins: Great. A couple clarifying questions: what percent of traffic is streaming interactive vs background batch?
[06:08] Evan Brooks: ~80% interactive/streaming, 20% background batch (summaries, nightly jobs).
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: Good to know. For background batch we can use larger batching windows to improve tokens/sec and lower cost.
[06:18] Dr. Priya Narang: What SLA are you looking for from Redwood in a production deployment?
[06:22] Maya Chen: We'd expect 99.9% uptime and targets on latency SLOs for core routes.
[06:27] Jamie Collins: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets with enterprise plans; we'll include SLA matrix in follow up.
[06:33] Evan Brooks: Any limitations on streaming concurrency per instance?
[06:37] Omar Aziz: We don't have a hard per-instance session cap, it's more about memory/KV size and aggregate compute. For long-context sessions memory can be the bottleneck. We account for KV cache size per session.
[06:49] Dr. Priya Narang: On quantization — how mature are your quantized kernels for 13B? We tried some third-party quantized models with hallucination regressions.
[06:58] Sofia Martinez: Our runtime supports multiple quantization profiles and we've validated them against accuracy regressions. We'll include recommended quantization profiles for your target models and the accuracy tradeoffs. If accuracy sensitivity is high we can prioritize higher-precision profiles.
[07:14] Evan Brooks: Can you show us an example of p95 telemetry? We want to see traces: time to first token, KV fetch, network, token generation.
[07:22] Jamie Collins: Yes — our Console shows per-route breakdown: time spent in queue/batching, model compute, network serialization, and per-token throughput. We'll attach screenshots and sample traces.
[07:33] Maya Chen: About cost — do you expose per-token cost with breakdown by compute vs infra?
[07:38] Jamie Collins: Yes. Redwood Console includes token-level cost breakdown and you can filter by model and route; the TCO workbook will show compute, infra, and additional support fees.
[07:47] Evan Brooks: We need an initial benchmark: 3 models (7B, 13B, 70B) with 32/128/1024 token scenarios across concurrencies 10/50/120. Can you run that?
[07:57] Sofia Martinez: We can run that as part of a Paid POC or as an initial free trial sample for small scale. For 70B we recommend Dedicated for production; Hosted can run it but cost and latency will be higher.
[08:09] Dr. Priya Narang: Timeline — we'd like to pilot in prod in 8-10 weeks if benchmarks look good.
[08:15] Jamie Collins: Reasonable. We'll aim to get benchmarks back within 7 business days after receiving sample prompts.
[08:21] Evan Brooks: Any troubleshooting when disruptions happen?
[08:24] Omar Aziz: We provide tracing hooks and error analysis in Console. Also automatic fallback routing policies.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Security question — does Redwood persist prompt/response plaintext for Hosted?
[08:36] Jamie Collins: By default we persist logs for troubleshooting; retention is configurable and can be disabled. For PHI you should use Dedicated/Private with customer-managed keys and disabled retention if required. We'll provide specifics in the security doc.
[08:51] Dr. Priya Narang: Ok. On the commercial side what's the pricing model for Dedicated versus Hosted?
[08:56] Jamie Collins: Hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding units; Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit and lower per-token execution cost plus infra fee. Private is license + infra. We'll include the pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[09:09] Evan Brooks: Can you include an estimate for token/sec per GPU for our workload in the TCO?
[09:13] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll include measured tokens/sec numbers and assumptions for batching and streaming.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Anything else from the team?
[09:21] Leo Park: Please include SOC2 report and details on KMS integration.
[09:25] Jamie Collins: Will do. Quick recap of next steps...
[09:28] Jamie Collins: Action items: Jamie send pricing + SOC2 + SLA matrix; Sofia to run benchmarks after we get sanitized prompts; Evan to deliver prompt set and confirm concurrency windows; schedule a deeper demo for streaming and KV cache.
[09:41] Dr. Priya Narang: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:44] Jamie Collins: Thanks all — we'll follow up over email with links and timeline.
[09:47] [call ends]
